fire: In the intensive care unit, the resident inserted two arterial lines before the surgery.
Poorly controlled diabetes damages the small vessels and impairs venous return from the legs.

A tourniquet left on too long will stop arterial supply to the whole limb.
The scan showed reduced perfusion through the coronary arteries during exercise.
Compression stockings improve venous circulation in patients who sit for long hours.
In the ward, nurses check the arterial line every hour for clots and leaks.
Raised orbital venous pressure can impair drainage of fluid from the eye.

Poorly controlled diabetes damages the kidneys and slows healing of wounds on the legs.
The orthopaedic surgeon measured bone density through a scan of the femur.
A splint left on too long will stiffen the joints of the whole limb.
The scan showed a small tear in the knee ligament after the fall.
Compression bandages reduce swelling in patients who sprain an ankle.
In the ward, nurses check the feeding tube every hour for blockages and leaks.
Raised pressure in the ear can cause dizziness and a ringing sound.
